quantity.name: curvature-driven shrinkage of an isolated circular grain
quantity.observable: Grain area from the integral of the order parameter, R = sqrt(A/pi). The law dR/dt = -M sigma / R integrates to R^2 = R0^2 - 2 M sigma t, exactly linear in t with a slope independent of R0.
quantity.supersedes: The polycrystal exponent fit is a statistical measurement that never left the transient: late-window fits gave about 0.06 against the target 0.5. The isolated circular grain tests the same curvature-driven kinetics as a sharp analytic statement instead.

reference.derivation: Allen-Cahn curvature-driven boundary migration: the normal velocity of a boundary is v = -M sigma kappa_curv, and for a circle kappa_curv = 1/R, giving dR/dt = -M sigma / R.
reference.absolute_slope_not_claimed: 2 M sigma is not compared in absolute terms. GBEvolution converts GBmob0 and GBenergy through its own length_scale, time_scale and eV bookkeeping; reproducing that conversion here would mean reverse-engineering the code under test and then checking it against itself. Every other assertion the law makes is verified independently.

tolerance.metric: maximum absolute deviation of the R^2(t) fit from linearity, expressed as 1 - R^2_corr
tolerance.rationale: Declared before the sweep. R^2 linear in t is the whole content of the curvature law; 0.001 corresponds to a correlation of 0.999.

convergence.mobility_levels: GBMobility overridden to M and 2M at the reference radius and mesh

slope_independent_of_R0.metric: relative spread of dR^2/dt across R0 = 120, 150, 180
slope_independent_of_R0.rationale: dR/dt proportional to 1/R is what makes the slope independent of the starting radius; this is the sharpest consequence of the law.

slope_proportional_to_mobility.rationale: Verifies the mobility scaling without needing GBEvolution's unit conversion: whatever the constant is, doubling the imposed GB mobility must double the slope exactly.

mesh_independence.metric: relative spread of dR^2/dt across nx = 75, 100, 150

fit_window.rationale: Fixed before the sweep. Above 0.95 the SmoothCircleIC profile is still relaxing to its equilibrium tanh shape; below 0.45 the radius approaches the 60-unit diffuse interface width and the sharp-interface law no longer applies.
